name: tally
description: Embed Tally.so forms as-is. Auto-loads Tally's embed.js on demand — no page-level scripts config needed. Form design (theme, layout, title) is controlled entirely in the Tally dashboard.
author: JasonJS Framework

TallyForm.description: Embeds a Tally.so form via iframe with optional dynamic height resizing via postMessage

formId.description: Tally form ID — found in the form share URL: tally.so/r/{formId}

height.description: Fallback height when dynamicHeight is false

dynamicHeight.description: Auto-resize iframe height based on form content (handled by Tally's embed.js)

ai_prompt:
# Tally Forms Addon ## When to Use Use the Tally addon to embed any Tally.so form into a page: - Contact forms - Waitlist signups - Surveys and feedback - Lead capture - Registration forms - Any form built at tally.so ## How to Get the formId The form ID is in the Tally share URL: - Share URL: `https://tally.so/r/nPvaKV` → formId = `nPvaKV` - Or from the embed code Tally provides ## Basic Usage (page JSON) ```json { "components": [ { "component": "@addons/tally/TallyForm", "attributes": { "formId": "nPvaKV", "title": "Contact Form" } } ] } ``` **Do NOT add a `scripts` field** to the page — this addon auto-loads Tally's `embed.js` internally (once per page, cached). ## Form Design Lives in Tally The form's theme, colors, layout, title visibility, background, and everything else visual is controlled in the Tally dashboard (Settings → Design). The embed inherits whatever you saved there. This addon intentionally does NOT pass any query parameters to the iframe — it just loads `https://tally.so/embed/{formId}` as-is. Previous versions exposed props like `alignLeft`, `hideTitle`, `transparentBackground` that tried to override Tally's design via URL params, but they fight with the form's own styling and cause rendering issues (washed-out colors, clipped content, mismatched backgrounds). The simple, reliable approach is: **design the form in Tally, embed it as-is**. If you need a different look, edit the form in Tally — it updates the embed automatically, no redeploy. ## In a User Component ```jsx import TallyForm from '@addons/tally/TallyForm'; const ContactSection = () => (

Get in Touch

); export default ContactSection; ``` ## Props Reference | Prop | Type | Default | Description | |------|------|---------|-------------| | `formId` | string | required | Tally form ID from the share URL | | `title` | string | `'Form'` | iframe title (accessibility) | | `height` | string | `'100vh'` | Fallback height when dynamicHeight is false | | `customHeight` | string | — | Fixed height override (e.g. `'600px'`) | | `dynamicHeight` | boolean | **true** | Auto-resize iframe to fit form (handled by Tally's embed.js via postMessage) | ## How It Works The component renders an iframe with `data-tally-src="https://tally.so/embed/{formId}"`, then loads `https://tally.so/widgets/embed.js` on mount and calls `Tally.loadEmbeds()`. Tally's script activates the iframe and handles dynamic height resizing via postMessage events. ## CSP Requirements For this to work, `next.config.js` must allow Tally in CSP: - `script-src` must include `https://tally.so` - `frame-src` must include `https://tally.so` Both are configured in the framework's next.config.js. ## Tips - `dynamicHeight: true` (default) handles multi-step forms that grow as users progress - For a fixed-size embed, set `dynamicHeight: false` and provide a `height` (e.g. `'700px'`) - The `allow` attribute on the iframe includes camera, microphone, and geolocation for forms that need those - **All visual customization happens in Tally** — this addon is a dumb embed wrapper by design
